title: Home & neighbourhood
goal: Rent a flat, deal with power cuts and leaks, complain politely to a landlord or a neighbour, get things fixed and move house.
intro:
Most young people in Kabul, Jalalabad or Peshawar who leave the family home end up renting: a flat (اپارتمان) in a new building, or a floor of someone's house. That means a landlord (د کور مالک), rent, a deposit, power cuts, an empty water tank in summer, a gas heater in winter — and neighbours.

In this unit you'll learn to talk about all of that, to **complain without giving offence** (soft first, then firm, and 'it's been three days that …'), and to say **who should fix it**: 'the landlord should fix it', 'it needs changing', 'get a plumber in'.

grammar.title: Complaining without giving offence: soft first, then firm
grammar.body:
A complaint in Pashto is a small negotiation, and the way you open it decides how it ends. Go in three steps.

**1. Soften.** Start with an apology or a condition, then say the problem: **بښنه غواړم، خو …** 'sorry, but …', **که زحمت نه وي …** 'if it's no trouble …', and finish requests with **مهرباني وکړئ**. Use **تاسو** and the polite imperative (-əy) with a landlord, a neighbour you don't know well, or anyone older — even if they call you ته. Among friends ته is fine.

**2. Say how long it has been: … کېږي چې …** English says 'it's been three days since …' or 'for three days'. Pashto says the time is 'becoming': **درې ورځې کېږي چې** اوبه نشته 'there's been no water for three days' (lit. three days are becoming that there's no water). The pattern is:

time + **کېږي** + **چې** + the situation in the **present** tense

يوه مياشت کېږي چې دلته **اوسېږم** 'I've been living here for a month'. English uses 'have been', but Pashto keeps the plain present, because the situation is still going on. The time word stays as it is (ورځې, اوونۍ, مياشت); کېږي does not change.

**3. Firm up if nothing happens.** **څو ځله مې درته وويل** 'I've told you several times' (ergative clitic مې + past), **دا بايد نن جوړ شي** 'this has to be fixed today', **نور صبر نه شم کولای** 'I can't wait any longer'.

**The trap:** don't jump to step 3. A direct 'your noise is too much' to a neighbour is a real insult in a culture built on honour (ننګ); the same complaint wrapped in بښنه غواړم and a smile gets results.

grammar.title: Who should fix it? دې, بايد … شي and getting someone in
grammar.body:
Unit 25 showed that Pashto uses the ordinary verb for 'getting things done'. At home the real question is **who** does the job. Five patterns cover it:

**1. 'He should … / let him …': دې + perfective** (the optative from unit 18). **مالک دې يې جوړ کړي** 'the landlord should fix it'. دې is a clitic: it sits after the first word or phrase, before يې.

**2. 'It needs …-ing': بايد + the کېدل side** (no doer at all). **نل بايد بدل شي** 'the pipe needs replacing', چت بايد جوړ شي 'the ceiling needs repairing'. Compare بايد بدل **يې کړې** 'you must replace it' — now there is a doer.

**3. 'Get someone in to …': X راوغواړه چې + subjunctive.** **مستري راوغواړه چې جوړ يې کړي** 'get a repairman in to fix it'. With a request to pass on: **مالک ته ووايه چې** … 'tell the landlord to …'.

**4. 'By someone': د X په لاس** (lit. by X's hand). قلف مې **د مستري په لاس** بدل کړ 'I had the lock changed by the repairman'. The verb is still the ordinary transitive one, ergative in the past.

**5. 'It's X's job to …': دا د X کار دی چې + subjunctive.**

**The trap:** after چې use the **perfective subjunctive** (کړي, شي, راشي), not the past: مستري ته مې وويل چې سبا **راشي** (not راغی) 'I told the repairman to come tomorrow'.

dialogue.setting: January in Kabul. Wais rents a flat in Taimani. The water tank is empty and the heater won't light, so he phones his landlord, Haji Sahib, while his friend Hamid listens in.

culture:
Renting in Kabul has its own customs. Rent is often quoted in dollars as well as afghanis, a few months are paid in advance, and many families use **ګرو** (garáw): instead of monthly rent the tenant lends the owner a large lump sum, lives in the house rent-free, and gets the whole sum back on leaving. Power cuts are part of life — people say **برق لاړ** / **برېښنا لاړه** 'the power's gone' and plan around a schedule; in Peshawar the same thing is **بجلي لاړه** or, in English, *load-shedding*. Water comes from a well or a tank on the roof, and in winter the whole family gathers round the **بخاري**.

An older landlord is addressed as **حاجي صاحب** or **کاکا** 'uncle' and with **تاسو**, even if he calls you ته and 'son'. With neighbours, relationships come first: when you move in, neighbours may send over food or tea, and it's good manners to return the plate with something on it. Complaints about noise, rubbish or parking are best made gently and in person, with بښنه غواړم, never by shouting from the balcony — a public scolding is an insult to the whole household.

tip.title: Renting words
tip.body:
- **کرايه** is rent (and a taxi fare); a place *to rent* is **د کرايې** کور / اپارتمان.
- Floors are counted with ordinals: په **درېيم** پوړ کې 'on the third floor'.
- **مياشتنی** 'monthly' agrees like any -ay adjective: مياشتنۍ کرايه (f).

tip.title: 'The power's gone': things that come and go
tip.body:
- Electricity 'goes' and 'comes': برېښنا **لاړه** / **راغله** — feminine past, because برېښنا is feminine (Kabul برق لاړ, masculine).
- Taps, tanks and heaters 'work' or 'don't work': **کار نه کوي**.
- **بند** 'off, shut' + کړه = turn it off: نل بند کړه.

lessons.title: Complaining politely

tip.title: Soft first: بښنه غواړم، خو … · … کېږي چې
tip.body:
- Open with **بښنه غواړم، خو …** or **که زحمت نه وي**, and use تاسو with a landlord.
- 'It's been X since …' = time + **کېږي چې** + present: درې ورځې **کېږي** چې اوبه نشته.
- Firmer: **څو ځله مې درته وويل** 'I've told you several times'.

sentences.native: که زحمت نه وي، نن يې وګورئ.
sentences.roman: ka zahmát na wi, nən ye wə́gorəy.
sentences.en: If it's no trouble, please have a look at it today.

sentences.native: يوه مياشت کېږي چې په دې کور کې اوسېږو.
sentences.roman: yáwa miyā́sht kéẓi che pə de kor ke oséẓu.
sentences.en: We've been living in this house for a month.

lessons.title: Who is going to fix it?

tip.title: 'He should fix it' · 'it needs fixing'
tip.body:
- **دې** + perfective: مالک **دې** يې جوړ کړي 'the landlord should fix it'.
- No doer: **بايد** + شي: نل بايد بدل **شي** 'the pipe needs replacing'.
- Getting someone in: مستري راوغواړه **چې** جوړ يې کړي.
- After چې use the subjunctive (کړي, راشي), never the past.
tip.pattern: X دې يې جوړ کړي · بايد … شي

new: دا د مالک کار دی چې جوړ يې کړي.

sentences.native: مالک دې يې جوړ کړي، زما کار نه دی.
sentences.roman: mālík de ye joṛ kṛi, zmā kār na day.
sentences.en: The landlord should fix it, it's not my job.

sentences.native: مستري راوغواړه چې نل جوړ کړي.
sentences.roman: mistrí rā́wəġwāṛa che nal joṛ kṛi.
sentences.en: Get a plumber in to fix the tap.

sentences.native: قلف بايد بدل شي.
sentences.roman: qulf bāyád badál shi.
sentences.en: The lock needs changing.

sentences.native: ما مستري ته وويل چې سبا راشي.
sentences.roman: mā mistrí ta wə́wayəl che sabā́ rā́shi.
sentences.en: I told the repairman to come tomorrow.

sentences.native: د تاوان پيسې څوک ورکوي، ته که مالک؟
sentences.roman: də tāwā́n páyse tsok warkawí, tə ka mālík?
sentences.en: Who pays for the damage, you or the landlord?

sentences.native: که مالک يې جوړ نه کړي، زه به يې خپله جوړ کړم.
sentences.roman: ka mālík ye joṛ na kṛi, zə ba ye xpə́la joṛ kṛəm.
sentences.en: If the landlord doesn't fix it, I'll fix it myself.

sentences.native: قلف مې د مستري په لاس بدل کړ.
sentences.roman: qulf me də mistrí pə lās badál kaṛ.
sentences.en: I had the lock changed by a repairman.

sentences.native: دا ستا کار نه دی، مالک ته ووايه.
sentences.roman: dā stā kār na day, mālík ta wə́wāya.
sentences.en: That's not your job — tell the landlord.

sentences.native: مستري وويل چې نل بايد بدل شي.
sentences.roman: mistrí wə́wayəl che nal bāyád badál shi.
sentences.en: The plumber said the pipe needs replacing.

sentences.native: تاوان ډېر نه دی، ژر به جوړ شي.
sentences.roman: tāwā́n ḍer na day, zhər ba joṛ shi.
sentences.en: The damage isn't bad, it'll be fixed soon.

lessons.title: Neighbours, noise and rubbish
new: زه نوی راغلی يم، ستاسو ګاونډی يم.
بښنه غواړم، خو شور مو لږ زيات دی.

sentences.native: دا سيمه ارامه ده؟
sentences.roman: dā síma ārā́ma da?
sentences.en: Is this a quiet area?

sentences.native: زه په دې کوڅه کې اوسېږم.
sentences.roman: zə pə de kútsa ke oséẓəm.
sentences.en: I live on this lane.

sentences.native: زموږ په کوڅه کې ډېر ماشومان دي.
sentences.roman: zmuẓ pə kútsa ke ḍer māshumā́n di.
sentences.en: There are lots of children on our lane.

sentences.native: ګاونډيان مو ښه خلک دي؟
sentences.roman: gāwnḍiyā́n mo ṣə xálək di?
sentences.en: Are your neighbours nice people?

sentences.native: د شپې شور مه کوئ، مهرباني وکړئ.
sentences.roman: də shpe shor ma kawə́y, mehrabāní wə́kṛəy.
sentences.en: Please don't make noise at night.

sentences.native: په خير راغلې! که څه ته اړتيا لرې، راته ووايه.
sentences.roman: pə xayr rā́ġle! ka tsə ta aṛtiyā́ lare, rā́ta wə́wāya.
sentences.en: Welcome! If you need anything, just tell me.

sentences.native: دلته خځلې چېرته واچوو؟
sentences.roman: dálta xazə́le chérta wā́chawu?
sentences.en: Where do we put the rubbish here?

sentences.native: خځلې په کوڅه کې مه اچوئ.
sentences.roman: xazə́le pə kútsa ke ma achawə́y.
sentences.en: Don't throw rubbish in the lane.

sentences.native: کډه کله کوئ؟
sentences.roman: kaḍá kə́la kawə́y?
sentences.en: When are you moving?

sentences.native: سامان مو ډېر دی؟
sentences.roman: sāmā́n mo ḍer day?
sentences.en: Have you got a lot of stuff?

sentences.native: سبا کډه کوو، ته راتلای شې چې مرسته وکړې؟
sentences.roman: sabā́ kaḍá kawú, tə rātlā́y she che mrásta wə́kṛe?
sentences.en: We're moving tomorrow — can you come and help?

sentences.native: د دې سيمې اوسېدونکي يو بل سره مرسته کوي.
sentences.roman: də de síme osedúnki yaw bəl sara mrásta kawí.
sentences.en: The people who live round here help each other.

sentences.native: هو، خامخا راځم.
sentences.roman: ho, xāmaxā́ rā́dzəm.
sentences.en: Yes, I'll definitely come.

sentences.native: دا سامان پورته يوسه.
sentences.roman: dā sāmā́n pórta yósa.
sentences.en: Take this stuff upstairs.

sentences.native: موټر ښکته په کوڅه کې دی.
sentences.roman: moṭár ṣkə́ta pə kútsa ke day.
sentences.en: The car's down in the lane.

sentences.native: يخچال ډېر دروند دی، يوازې يې نه شم وړلای.
sentences.roman: yaxchā́l ḍer drund day, yawā́ze ye na shəm wṛə́lāy.
sentences.en: The fridge is really heavy, I can't carry it on my own.

sentences.native: پورته پوړ کې يوه کورنۍ اوسېږي.
sentences.roman: pórta poṛ ke yáwa kornə́y oséẓi.
sentences.en: A family lives on the floor above.

sentences.native: کډه مو وکړه؟ نوی کور مو چېرته دی؟
sentences.roman: kaḍá mo wə́kṛa? náway kor mo chérta day?
sentences.en: Have you moved? Where's your new place?
